from.place: proof, part (2): the affine calculation behind the assertion that the complement of an effective Cartier divisor is scheme-theoretically dense

title: A principal nonzerodivisor complement is scheme-theoretically dense
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $a\in A$ be a non-zero-divisor. For the affine scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme] and the principal open $U=D(a)\subseteq X$ with inclusion $j:U\to X$, the restriction morphism $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective, and $U$ is topologically dense in $X$.
